I am 67 years old. I never went to school, not one day. I have farmed for 45 years in Quzhou. I learned everything from my mother and from watching the fields with my own eyes. I have 33 mu, which is a lot of land for two old people, but during busy times I hire workers from the village and my nephew brings his machine to help. I do not read books and I do not trust outsiders who tell me what to do. I trust what I saw work on my own field and on my neighbors' fields.

Last year, my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu and my maize gave about 1300 jin per mu. I used the same fertilizer as always, and it worked, so this year I will do the same. I never start from nothing. I start from last year and change only if I saw someone else do better.

For my wheat, I plant 30 mu. I use the improved wheat seeds that Lao Zhang used — his field was the greenest in the village last year. Before planting, I till with the rotary machine. I put one big bag of the three-kind fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer, and then I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu. The dealer's bags are the standard big ones. I water three times: once after planting if the sky stays dry, once when the wheat is getting tall, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice, once for grass and once for bugs. I expect about 1000 jin per mu again.

For summer maize, I plant the same 30 mu right after cutting the wheat in June. I use hybrid seeds, the ones in the yellow bags from the dealer. I do not till the soil for maize — there is no time, and the machine plants directly into the wheat stubble. I put half a bag of the three-kind fertilizer and half a bag of urea per mu. I water twice, three times if the summer is very hot and dry. I spray twice. I expect about 1200 to 1300 jin per mu.

For cotton, I keep 3 mu. Cotton is hard work, bending over all day, but it brings cash money. I plough the cotton field deep in spring. I use improved cotton seeds. Cotton is picky and needs more food and medicine than grain. I put one bag of the three-kind fertilizer, half a bag of urea, and half a bag of that white potash fertilizer per mu. The dealer told me cotton likes the white one, and I saw that Lao Wang's cotton looked strong when he used it. I water three times and spray four times because the bollworm always comes. I expect about 200 jin of clean cotton per mu.

I worry about costs every time I buy fertilizer. Each bag is real money out of my pocket. But two years ago my cousin tried to save on fertilizer and his wheat grew short like grass. He lost half his crop. I would rather spend too much on fertilizer than risk that. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I also watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Zhang buys more this year, I buy more. If he tries a new seed and it looks good, maybe I will try it next year, but not this year. This year I stick with what I know, because change is risky when you are my age.
